description_en: Situated at the northern part of the Dupāt Square and to the east of the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Temple (LAL2110), this long Capāḥ is now called the Sanāḥ Guṭhī Chẽ.Standing impressively tall, it stretches to fill almost two-thirds of the open space in front of the building. Dāphā Bhajana Phalcāis located to its west, whilst Picū Phalcā stands opposite. The narrow alley towards the west of Dupāt Capāḥ leads to Subahāḥ, if further followed north. A private house to the north is now attached to it, open only to the east (at its front).Gutschow(2001, p. 639) writes that "the house of the death association was replaced by a monstrous four-storeyed structure in reinforced concrete in 1999. The two-storeyed house for the performance of music was replaced by an even larger structure in 2004 to accommodate a primary school sponsored by 'Mitra Japan'."Previously (until the 1990s), this monument was a two-storey Phalcā with a tiled roof and 14 bays. An image of Nāsaḥdyaḥ was once placed on its first floor. A small section of the old Dupāt Capāḥ can be seen in a photo in Carl Pruscha's Kathmandu Valley II, which shows that the tiled roof of the Sanāḥ Guṭhī Chẽ was attached to the second tier of the Gaṇeśa Temple. The photo, which Pruscha uses to describe the Dupāt Gaṇeśa, also shows that Kṛṣaka Pustakālaya (the library currently housed in the Pichū Phalcā) was still operating from this building back then (PruschaII, 1975: 188).Before this, the monument was a twelve-bayed phalcā,making it one of the longest in Patan. Kotpati (LAL4126) was located on the ground floor of a two-bay deep Capāḥ.Around 300 Maharjan families were associated with the Phalcā. However, Dupāt Capāḥ was was dismantled in 2004 and replaced by a four-storey highconcrete structure with seven bays and concrete pillars. It is now part of a larger building, and the Sanāḥ Guṭhī Chẽ today represents over 450 members of the funeralguthiof Dupāt Ṭola. The four-storey building has a verandah-like structure extending from all of its three upper floors. The ground floor is open on two sides (to the south and west). However, the western side of the ground floor is almost completely blocked by the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira.Vajrācārya(VS 2056, 164) has referred to thiscapāḥas Nāṭyeśvara Temple due to the fact that a statue of Nāsaḥdyaḥ has been enshrined on the second floor. Alongside other deities, newly installed images ofAṣṭamātṛkācan be seen on the outer sides of the concrete pillars of the building. However, it appears that these images have neither been consecrated nor are they worshipped; they seem to serve more of an aesthetic purpose.In July 2015, an image of Nāmasaṅgīti Mañjuśrī was installed in a narrow space between the shrine of Gaṇeśa and the main door of the Guṭhī Chẽ. The original two-storey building had a shrine of Nāsaḥdyaḥ on the upper floor; this was relocated to the second floor after the structure was rebuilt.Altogether, seven inscriptions have been attached to the wall of the ground floor. But they do not appear to be related to Dupāt Capāḥ. Two of the inscriptions are no longer legible, three of them are partially legible, and two remain in good condition. The transliteration and interpretation of four of these inscriptions is included below.
description_ne: दुपाः चोकको उत्तरपट्टि रहेको यो लामो चपाःलाई सनाः गुठी छेँ पनि भनिन्छ । दुपाः गणेश मन्दिरको पूर्वपट्टि रहेको यो चपाः चोकको लम्बाइको लगभग दुई तिहाइ भागमा लम्बिएर रहेको छ । दुफा भजन फल्चा यसको पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको छ भने पिचु फल्चा यसको अगाडि रहेको छ । यो चपाःको पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको गल्लीहुँदै उत्तरतिर जाँदा सौबाहा पुगिन्छ । पश्चिमपट्टि यो चपाः निजी घरसँग जोडिएको छ । यसको अगाडिको अथवा पूर्वी मोहडा मात्र खुला छ, अरूतर्फ अन्य संरचनासँग जोडिएको छ ।२०४६ सालसम्म यो चपाः टायलको छाना भएको दुईतले, १४ वटा कवल भएको फल्चाको रूपमा थियो । नासःद्यःको मूर्ति पहिला पहिलो तलामा राखिएको थियो । कार्ल प्रुस्चाको पुस्तक (१९७५ II : १८८) मा छापिएको फोटोमा दुपात गणेश मन्दिरको पछाडिपट्टि यो फल्चा देखिन्छ र अहिले पिछु फल्चा रहेको ठाउँमा त्यतिबेला कृषक पुस्तकालय रहेको थियो भन्ने कुरा त्यहाँ रहेको साइनबोर्डले देखाउँछ । अहिलेको पिछु फल्चा त्यति वेला त्यस भवनको पछाडिपट्टि रहेको थियो ।सन् २०१५ जुलाइमा गणेश मन्दिर र गुठीछेँ को मूल ढोकाको बीचको साँघुरो ठाउँमा नामसङ्गीति मञ्जुश्रीको प्रतिमा स्थापना गरियो । पहिला दुईतले फल्चा भवनको माथिल्लो तलामा नासःद्यःको पूजाकोठा थियो । पुनर्निर्माणपछि नासःद्यःको पूजाकोठा दोस्रो तलामा सारिएको छ । नयाँ भवनको सिमेन्टका स्तम्भहरूमा अष्टमातृका आदि देवताहरूको प्रतिमा बनाइएको छ ।यस चपाःको भुइँतलाको भितामा सातवटा शिलालेखहरू टाँसेर राखिएका छन् । ती मध्ये, दुई वटा पढ्न सकिने हालतमा छैनन्, तीनवटा आंशिक रूपमा पढ्न सकिने छन् भने दुई वटा राम्रो अवस्थामा छन् । चारवटा शिलालेखको पाठ र विवरण तल दिइएको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Installation of an Gaṇeśa image inside the Dupāḥ Gaṇeśa Mandira
historical_events.event_description: A stoneGaṃśalawas installed in thecapāḥ.Dhanavajra Bajracharya(2056) has interpreted this as beingGaneśa. The name of thethakāliis given as Parīdeva Bhāvo. The inscription is attached to the wall of the ground floor.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a stone toraṇa and matakārana in Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira and formation of a group of devotees.
historical_events.event_description: This historical event is related to the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira (LAL2110). For more details see the historical events of the monument.

Around VS 2040-45, members of the local Jyāpu community established a library in this Capāḥ. The photo published by Pruscha (1975 II: 188) used for describing the Dupāt Gaṇeśa also shows the board of the library.The library is currently housed in the Pichū Phalcā at the rear of the same building.

historical_events.event_name: Regulation of irrigation management in a rural area of eastern Lalitpur and the Sanāḥ Guṭh's role in this
historical_events.event_description: This inscription is attached to the eastern wall of the first floor. The historical event mentioned in this inscription is not related to thiscapāḥ. Rather, the inscription mentions the rules and regulations around the management of an irrigation canal in a rural area of eastern Lalitpur. This is the responsibility of the Sanāḥ Guṭhī. The text in this inscription has been partly copied from the inscription dated NS 803 referring to King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur. The same text is also mentioned inNepālikabhūpavaṁśāvalī(19.1.116a/I).
This inscription is attached to the wall of the ground floor. This inscription is no longer legible.
